summary: Brick tower on Southern Island at the entrance to Tenants Harbor, Maine: built 1857, first lit 1858, discontinued 1933, privately owned since, not open to the public.

corrections.why: USLHS gives the light 27 feet (8.2 m) above mean high water, and LighthouseFriends gives 27 feet. The record value of 20 m is not supported by the sources read.

USLHS gives 25 feet (7.6 m) from base to the center of the lantern. The NRHP nomination says just over 27 feet from base to lantern center, so the true figure is open. Proposed value follows the USLHS record; a human should check the NRHP figure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The USLHS record and the record file give 1857 (year established and year the original lens was installed). LighthouseFriends says the light was first lit on January 1, 1858. The NRHP nomination gives 1857 for the tower and the station. The story gives both dates.

The NRHP says the tower is just over 27 feet from its base to the center of the lantern. USLHS gives 27 feet above mean high water and 25 feet from base to lantern center; LighthouseFriends says 27 feet. The record gives 20 m (65 ft) for the focal height, which the sources do not support.

The Lighthouse Service Bulletin gives the tow of two disabled motor boats as September 17 and 18, 1914. LighthouseFriends dates a tow of two disabled boats to 1915. The story uses the 1914 Bulletin and notes LighthouseFriends.
The 1914 Bulletin spells the station Tennant Harbor, and LighthouseFriends lists several variants. The record and the roster use Tenants Harbor.

notes_for_editor: Sources read: the NRHP nomination (OCR text; the quotes checked against it, which is clean for these passages); the USLHS place record and roster (13 lines, matched to the station by name and position at 0.11 km); LighthouseFriends (copyrighted: paraphrased; the inspector's remark and the coal-delivery memory are quoted or paraphrased from it, and its underlying Lighthouse Digest articles were not read); the Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1914 p. 44 (OCR columns interleaved; the Jellison sentence reads cleanly). The Light-House Board and Commissioner reports in the corpus have no 'Tenants Harbor' hits under this spelling (searched with the variants). Newspapers were not searched for this station, so the 1933 sale and the 1914-1918 towing rest on the Bulletin and LighthouseFriends. The keeper names and spans are the USLHS archive's own roster lines. Living people: the current owner is not named. Andrew Wyeth (1978 purchase) and his wife Betsy are named as published (LighthouseFriends), in their public roles as painters and owners. Walter Whitehead (owner 1953-1978) is named as published. The 1935 buyers are named as published (LighthouseFriends). The story gives no private residence details. The record's structure height (8.0 m) and focal height (20.0 m) are proposed for correction; see corrections. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-27 (independent pass): Two disagreements the earlier draft did not state are now in the story. (1) Size of the island: LighthouseFriends gives about 22 acres, and the NRHP nomination gives approximately 20 acres for the nominated property. (2) Height: the NRHP nomination and LighthouseFriends give a tower of just over 27 feet (base to lantern center), while the USLHS record gives 25 feet from base to lantern center (and 27 feet light height above mean high water). The 1914 Bulletin's 'Tennant Harbor' spelling is quoted as the Bulletin prints it (PDF p. 44, OCR columns interleaved). Living-people check: Myron Corbett (son of keeper Willie W. Corbett, 1920-1923) and June Dudley (daughter of keeper Leonard B. Dudley, 1923-1933) are named as LighthouseFriends prints them; their connection with the station ended before about 1960. Andrew and Betsy Wyeth and Walter Whitehead are named as published. The current owner (LighthouseFriends names the painter Jamie Wyeth) is not named in the story. Not checked: the Light-House Board volumes (no Tenants Harbor hit in the corpus under this spelling, per the earlier note), and the 1933 sale's buyer names beyond LighthouseFriends.
